title: Acceleration of Free Electrons by Photonic Time-Crystals
authors: Lior Bar-Hillel, Alexey Gorlach, Ido Kaminer, Mordechai Segev
abstract: We study the quantum interaction between free electrons and photons in a time-varying media, and find that periodic modulation exponentially amplifies electron-photon coupling within momentum gaps, enabling arbitrarily large momentum transfer. By preparing the light in a two-mode squeezed vacuum state, the electron momentum grows faster than its spectral spreading, establishing time-modulated photonic media as a platform for accelerating free-electrons and shaping their quantum state.
summary: The paper demonstrates that Photonic Time-Crystals (PTCs) can dramatically enhance the coupling between free electrons and photons by exploiting exponentially growing field modes within photonic band gaps. This enhancement allows researchers to deterministically control the momentum kick imparted to electrons, opening a new quantum platform for shaping electron wavefunctions.
main_problem: The study investigates how quantum interactions between free electrons and photons are modified when the photonic environment is periodically modulated using Photonic Time-Crystals (PTCs). The goal is to use this modulation to control electron momentum transfer.
main_result: PTCs enable exponentially enhanced, controllable coupling for electron-light scattering, allowing for arbitrarily large and deterministically controlled momentum kicks to free electrons. Furthermore, nonclassical light states allow the momentum uncertainty to grow slower than the mean recoil, enabling directional wavefunction shaping.
method: The analysis uses a time-dependent Hamiltonian approach, employing Bogoliubov transformations to track photon field evolution in the presence of PTCs and deriving an effective scattering operator for electron interaction.
model_or_system: The system models free electrons propagating along $z$ interacting with photons confined by a periodically modulated refractive index (PTC). The dynamics are governed by a Hamiltonian involving free electron, time-dependent photonic, and interaction terms.
key_observables: Photon number ($\langle N(t) angle$), effective coupling strengths ($g_{\pm k}$), mean momentum transfer ($\langle \Delta p angle$), and the post-interaction electron spectrum $P(\Delta p)$.
important_parameters: PTC modulation period ($T_{PTC}$), interaction time, and the initial state of light (e.g., Two-Mode Squeezed Vacuum).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system can be described by an effective scattering operator derived from the full Hamiltonian, and that the Bogoliubov coefficients govern the field dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate PTC bandstructures showing momentum gaps where exponential growth of photon number occurs. They also show electron spectra exhibiting pronounced sideband ladders inside these gaps, demonstrating controlled wavefunction shaping via mean recoil vs. uncertainty plots.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical model using PTCs and the Hamiltonian. It then analyzes the Bogoliubov dynamics to show exponential field enhancement in momentum gaps. Finally, it applies this framework to derive an effective scattering operator for electron-light interaction (PINEM), demonstrating control over mean recoil and quantum state shaping.
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from Floquet engineering/PTCs with fundamental quantum optics problems like light-matter interaction, providing a novel platform for coherent energy/momentum transfer in condensed matter physics that has implications for ultrafast science.
